# **1. INTRODUCTION TO THE INTERNATIONAL COPPER STUDY GROUP AND ICSG INDUSTRY ADVISORY PANEL** 

The Industry Advisory Panel met on 14 October in London with the objective of encouraging further industry participation and informing a wider range of copper industry representatives of the work and benefits of the Study Group. Industry advisers from Australia, Chile, Finland, Germany, Japan, Mexico, Poland, Portugal, Spain, United Kingdom and the United States were present along with industry association and Study Group representatives. 

The Chairman opened the proceedings by informing the participants that the Industry Advisory Panel provides an opportunity for industry advisers to meet as a group, raise issues to the attention of government members and provide feedback, guidance and advice to the Group on its priorities, programs and activities. 

ICSG Secretary-General provided the Panel with a brief overview of the mandate of the Study Group and the role of the IAP. The Panel was then presented with information about selected 

publications and key recent and current ICSG work items including the results of the 2010/2011 Forecast presented in Antofagasta, recent publication of the Directory of Copper Mines and Plants, the Directory of Semis Fabricators and the Scrap Research Project Final Report. 

The Panel was also informed about ongoing and potential ICSG projects, including the establishment of the ICSG online statistical database, expanded coverage for the data on copper mines (Directory), leading indicators of refined copper use, and the copper semis capacity database. 

# **2. OUTCOMES OF THE SEPTEMBER 2010 IAP MEETING IN ANTOFAGASTA, CHILE** 

The secretariat provided the Panel with info

rmation on the topics presented and discussed at the IAP meeting that took place on the 28<sup>th</sup> September in Antofagasta, Chile. 

A summary was presented on the Survey of Regulatory Developments Affecting Copper and it was suggested by panellists that ICSG could also seek industry views and not only governments’ views, that ICSG could work more closely with the EU on this topic, and that the issue of a probable change in Russian copper export duties should be included in the survey. 

Participants were also informed that ICSG released the 2010 World Copper Factbook in September and a copy was distributed to participants. 

A summary of the results of the research undertaken on Leading Indicators for Refined Copper Usage was presented as well as a summary of the preliminary research on Global Exploration and Investment.  On the latter topic Mr Schonenberger from ECI highlighted the fact that what is more important and what end-users ask before investing in new copper intensive products is if there is enough copper in the future (10-20 years horizon) and that it is important to look at the new copper projects.  Mr Salaria of BHP Billiton and Dr Loveitt, IAP Chairman, suggested looking at the work being done by USGS on reserves and resources.  Mr Salaria also suggested looking at the factors that determine which mines will come on stream.  Mrs Finney from Aurubis said that it is also important in terms of copper availability to look at stocks held by funds, ETFs, and stocks that will not be available to the market. Mr Salaria asked if ICSG will do work on ETFs and the Secretary-General advised that it could very likely be an issue to be analysed by ICSG. 

Key topics affecting copper supply and demand were also presented by the secretariat based on Jon Barnes (CRU) presentation made at the Antofagasta meetings on _Longer Term Supply and Demand Issues and Factors Affecting Global Copper Markets_ . 

The secretariat also provided the Panel with information regarding the result of the survey conducted at the Antofagasta meeting on key issues for possible ICSG attention.  A table was presented ranking the issues in terms of how important it would be to have further work generated by ICSG (based on the results of the survey). 

**3. VIEWS OF PARTICIPANTS ON WHAT WORK THE STUDY GROUP SHOULD BE DOING** 

The Chairman invited the Panel to make any suggestions for specific work items and to comment on the results of the survey referred to above. 

There was a general discussion regarding the items ranked in the survey mainly focused on how ICSG could add value by working on specific topics. It was stressed that ICSG should avoid duplication with work undertaken by other entities.  Mr Bennett questioned the capability of ICSG to undertake all of the projects with limited staff and resources and suggested that ICSG should focus more on what it is strong at. The Secretary-General said that some topics had been listed with the aim of evaluating the inte

rest of member countries and industry and that it was not proposed all of these topics would be addressed; if ICSG were to conduct work in these areas it would complement and not duplicate work already being done elsewhere. 

Mr Salaria suggested that work on ETFs should be a priority topic of possible ICSG activity, for example by synthesising the views of others in this area. He noted that the LME is concerned about this topic and is undertaking a lot of work.  Mr Schonenberger inquired if it was realistic for ICSG to do analysis of ETFs and suggested that banks, although perhaps not impartial, were best placed to do it. The Secretary-General said that one possible way of ICSG addressing ETFs would be to bring together several speakers with different views on what is happening, and hold a panel discussion supported by a factual secretariat background document. 

Regarding views on further work on scrap, the panel members indicated that it would be of interest to have ICSG continuing its work on scrap, suggesting that regular updates are needed because the scrap market is so volatile.  It was agreed that industry would indicate at the April 2011 meeting what they think should be regularly updated so that ICSG could assess the periodicity of the updates based on the availability of data. In the discussion Mr Salaria suggested that ICSG should move to reporting demand not apparent usage, and that data on the use of scrap by semis should be included in the Bulletin. 

Asked about possible Study Group work on technology affecting copper production the interest was low as information was considered to be already available from many other sources. Asked about work on by-products interest was again low amongst participants as this is not considered a main driver in the copper industry. 

Mr Hedin from Luvata UK Ltd suggested that ICSG should list for each survey topic what are the aspects where further work is needed, and who is already active or doing work on these topics.  Dr Loveitt inquired if these topics could be further developed.  He suggested that ICSG presents a document on who is already analysing these items, how ICSG can bring additional value, and how it is feasible for ICSG to do the work with limited resources.  Dr Loveitt also proposed this to be the sole point in the agenda for discussions at the April meeting.  The Secretary-General referred to the active ICA/IWCC role in end-use analysis and indicated that ICSG’s role in this area could be to reinforce what others are doing and help disseminate the results.  Mr Bennett confirmed that a lot of work has been done by ICA on end-use. Mr Harris agreed that end-use is well covered by others and could not see how ICSG can add additional value.  Mr Bennett expressed the view that ICSG’s strength is historical data. 

The Secretary-General informed panel members that the next meeting of the IAP would take place in Lisbon in the week beginning 11 April 2011 (in the afternoon of Thursday 14 Ap

ril). 

The Chairman thanked all those in attendance for their valuable input to the work of the Study Group and adjourned the meeting.
